To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
networks enable the learning necessary for organizations to implement fundamental change.
social networks make the difference in the capability to implement fundamental organizational changes.
social networks make an important contribution to the capability of organizations for implementing fundamental organizational change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, How do social networks enable organizations to implement fundamental change?
the relationship between social networks, learning, and fundamental organizational change.
the role of networks in fundamental organizational change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
networks are important to organizational change and that a mixture of organization-wide networks, local networks, and local self-design networks are important for successful organizational change.
the role of networks in fundamental organizational change is to facilitate learning.
the role of networks in change implementation depends on the type of change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
networks are critical for organizations to learn and implement fundamental organizational change.
networks are important in fundamental change implementation, and that the more diverse and abundant the networks the better.
the role of networks in fundamental organizational change is to enable local learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

organizations need to develop networks of relationships that are not only information-sharing networks but also networks that enable the exchange and combination of knowledge and that facilitate local self-design.
networks are important for change implementation, but the type of network that is important is different for each stage in the change process and for different types of change.

organizations can be more successful at implementing fundamental organizational change by creating a learning network that includes a diversity of connections across organizational levels, both internal and external to the organization, and strong and weak ties.
